title.zh: 卷二八 補列傳第二十 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶
title.en: Volume 28 Biographies 20: Yuan Tan (Eastern Wei); Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao (Eastern Wei)
title.raw: 卷二八 補列傳第二十 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶 Volume 28 Biographies 20: Yuan Tan (Eastern Wei); Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao (Eastern Wei)

sentences.zh: 元坦 元斌 元孝友 元暉業 元弼 元韶

translations.literal: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan; Yuan Bin; Yuan Xiaoyou; Yuan Huiye; Yuan Bi; Yuan Shao

sentences.zh: 元坦，祖魏獻文皇帝，咸陽王禧第七子。

translations.literal: Yuan Tan — his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei; seventh son of Prince Xianyang Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan's grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei; he was the seventh son of Prince Xianyang Xi.

sentences.zh: 禧誅後，兄翼、樹等五人相繼南奔，故坦得承襲，改封敷城王。

translations.literal: After Xi was executed, his elder brothers Yi, Shu, and five others fled south in succession, so Tan was able to inherit; his fief was changed to Prince of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi was executed, his elder brothers Yi, Shu, and five others fled south one after another, so Tan inherited the title; his fief was changed to prince of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 永安初，復本封咸陽郡王，累遷侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was restored to his original enfeoffment as Prince of Xianyang commandery; he rose through repeated promotions to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an he was restored to his original enfeoffment as prince of Xianyang commandery and rose through repeated promotions to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 莊帝從容謂曰：「「王才非荀、蔡，中歲屢遷，當由少長朕家，故有超授。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang said to him at ease: ""Prince, your talent is not like Xun or Cai; in your middle years you have been repeatedly transferred — this must be because you grew up young in my household, hence the extraordinary promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said to him at ease, "Prince, your talent is not like that of Xun or Cai; yet in mid-career you have been repeatedly promoted. That must be because you grew up in my household from youth — hence these extraordinary appointments.

sentences.zh: 」初，禧死後，諸子貧乏，坦兄弟為彭城王勰所收養，故有此言。

translations.literal: " Earlier, after Xi died his sons were impoverished; Tan and his brothers were taken in and raised by Prince Pengcheng Xie — hence this remark.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, after Xi died his sons were impoverished; Tan and his brothers were taken in and raised by Prince Pengcheng Xie — hence this remark.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，其兄樹見禽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, his elder brother Shu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, his elder brother Shu was captured.

sentences.zh: 坦見樹既長且賢，慮其代己，密勸朝廷以法除之。

translations.literal: Tan saw that Shu was both older and worthy, and feared Shu would replace him; he secretly urged the court to eliminate Shu by law.
translations.idiomatic: Tan saw that Shu was older and more worthy and feared he would be displaced; he secretly urged the court to eliminate Shu by law.

sentences.zh: 樹知之，泣渭坦曰：「我往因家難，不能死亡，寄食江湖，受其爵命。

translations.literal: When Shu learned of it, he wept at the Wei River and said to Tan: "I once, because of family calamity, could not die; I lived on others' food on rivers and lakes and accepted their ranks and commands.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu learned of it, he wept on the Wei River and said to Tan, "Long ago, because of our family's calamity, I could not die; I lived on others' food along rivers and lakes and accepted their ranks and commands.

sentences.zh: 今者之來，非由義至，求活而已，豈望榮華。

translations.literal: My coming now is not from righteousness — I seek only to live; how could I hope for glory.
translations.idiomatic: My coming now is not from righteousness — I seek only to live. How could I hope for glory?

sentences.zh: 汝何肆其猜忌，忘在原之義，腰背雖偉，善無可稱。

translations.literal: Why do you indulge your suspicions and forget the bond of kin from one root? Though your back and waist are imposing, your goodness is nothing worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Why do you indulge your suspicions and forget the bond of those from one root? Though your back and waist are imposing, there is no goodness in you worth praising.

sentences.zh: 」坦作色而去。

translations.literal: " Tan flushed and left.
translations.idiomatic: " Tan flushed and left.

sentences.zh: 樹死，竟不臨哭。

translations.literal: When Shu died, Tan never went to mourn at his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu died, Tan never went to mourn at his coffin.

sentences.zh: 坦歷司徒、太尉、太傅，加侍中、太師、錄尚書事、宗正、司州牧。

translations.literal: Tan held the posts of Minister over the Masses, Grand Commandant, and Grand Tutor, with additional posts as palace attendant, grand preceptor, recorder of the masters of writing, director of imperial clan affairs, and governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tan served as minister over the masses, grand commandant, and grand tutor, with additional posts as palace attendant, grand preceptor, recorder of the masters of writing, director of imperial clan affairs, and governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 雖祿厚位尊，貪求滋甚，賣獄鬻官，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Though his salary was rich and his rank exalted, his greed grew ever worse; he sold judgments and traded offices without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Though his salary was rich and his rank exalted, his greed grew ever worse; he sold judgments and traded offices without limit.

sentences.zh: 為御史劾奏免官，以王歸第。

translations.literal: The censorate impeached him and he was dismissed from office; he returned to his estate as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate impeached him and he was dismissed; he returned to his estate as a prince.

sentences.zh: 尋起為特進，出為冀州刺史，專復聚斂。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as special eminence, sent out as inspector of Jizhou, and again devoted himself to extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as special eminence and sent out as inspector of Jizhou, where he again devoted himself to extortion.

sentences.zh: 每百姓納賦，除正稅外，別先責絹五疋，然後為受。

translations.literal: Whenever the common people paid taxes, aside from the regular tax he first exacted an extra five bolts of silk, and only then would accept payment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the common people paid taxes, aside from the regular levy he first exacted five extra bolts of silk per household, and only then would accept payment.

sentences.zh: 性好畋漁，無日不出，秋冬獵雉兔，春夏捕魚蟹，鷹犬常數百頭。

translations.literal: He loved hunting and fishing; not a day passed without going out — in autumn and winter he hunted pheasants and hares, in spring and summer he caught fish and crabs; his hawks and dogs numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting and fishing and went out every day without exception — in autumn and winter he hunted pheasants and hares, in spring and summer he caught fish and crabs; his hawks and dogs numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 自言寧三日不食，不能一日不獵。

translations.literal: He said himself that he would rather go three days without food than one day without hunting.
translations.idiomatic: He said himself that he would rather go three days without food than one day without hunting.

sentences.zh: 入為太傅。

translations.literal: He entered court as grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初準例降爵，封新豐縣公，除特進、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, per precedent his rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed Duke of Xinfeng county and appointed special eminence and commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao under Qi, per precedent his rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed duke of Xinfeng county and appointed special eminence and commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 坐子世寶與通直散騎侍郎彭貴平因酒醉誹謗，妄說圖讖，有司奏當死，詔並宥之。

translations.literal: Because his son Shibao and the attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Peng Guiping, in drunkenness, slandered and rashly spoke of portents and prophecy, the authorities memorialized that they should die; an edict pardoned them both.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son Shibao and the attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Peng Guiping, while drunk, slandered the court and rashly spoke of portents and prophecy, the authorities memorialized that they should die; an edict pardoned them both.

sentences.zh: 坦配北營州，死配所。

translations.literal: Tan was consigned to northern Yingzhou; he died in the place of his assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was consigned to northern Yingzhou and died in the place of his assignment.

sentences.zh: 元斌，字善集，祖魏獻文皇帝。

translations.literal: Yuan Bin, styled Shanjii, his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bin, styled Shanjii — his grandfather was Emperor Xianwen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 父高陽王雍，從孝莊於河陰遇害。

translations.literal: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang at Heyin and met disaster there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Prince Gaoyang Yong followed Emperor Xiaozhuang to Heyin and met disaster there.

sentences.zh: 斌少襲祖爵，歷位侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Bin in youth inherited his grandfather's title; he held posts including palace attendant and left vice director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Bin in youth inherited his grandfather's title and held posts including palace attendant and left vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 斌美儀貌，性寬和，居官重慎，頗為齊文襄愛賞。

translations.literal: Bin had fine appearance; his nature was mild and broad; in office he was cautious and weighty — Gao Cheng greatly loved and appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had fine looks; his nature was mild and broad; in office he was cautious and weighty — Gao Cheng greatly loved and appreciated him.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，準例降爵，為高陽縣公，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, per precedent his rank was reduced; he became Duke of Gaoyang county and was appointed right grand master for the brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao under Qi, per precedent his rank was reduced; he became duke of Gaoyang county and was appointed right grand master for the brilliant.

sentences.zh: 二年，從文宣討契丹還，至白狼河，以罪賜死。

translations.literal: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Emperor Wenxuan, at the Bailang River he was ordered to die for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Gao Yang, at the Bailang River he was ordered to die for his crime.

sentences.zh: 元孝友，祖魏太武皇帝。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiaoyou — his grandfather was Emperor Taiwu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 兄臨淮王彧無子，令孝友襲爵。

translations.literal: His elder brother Prince Huaihuai Yu had no son; he had Xiaoyou inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Prince Huaihuai Yu had no son; Xiaoyou was made to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 累遷滄州刺史，為政溫和，好行小惠，不能清白，而無所侵犯，百姓亦以此便之。

translations.literal: He rose through repeated promotions to inspector of Cangzhou; his governance was mild and harmonious, he liked to do small favors; he could not be upright but did not violate or harass others — the common people found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to inspector of Cangzhou; his governance was mild and harmonious, and he liked to do small favors. He could not be upright, yet he did not violate or harass others — the common people found this convenient.

sentences.zh: 魏靜帝宴文襄於華林，孝友因醉自譽，又云：「陛下許賜臣能。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Gao Cheng at Hualin; Xiaoyou, drunk, praised himself, and also said: "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei feasted Gao Cheng at Hualin; Xiaoyou, drunk, praised himself and also said, "Your Majesty promised to grant me ability.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「朕恒聞王自道清。

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed and said: "I constantly hear the Prince speak of his own integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "I constantly hear the Prince speak of his own integrity.

sentences.zh: 」文襄曰：「臨淮王奉旨舍罪。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng said: "Prince Huaihuai received the decree and is pardoned of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng said, "Prince Huaihuai has received the decree and is pardoned of guilt.

sentences.zh: 」於是君臣俱笑而不罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon ruler and ministers all laughed and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 孝友明於政理，嘗奏表曰：

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was clear in governing principles; he once submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou was skilled in governance; he once submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 令制：百家為黨族，二十家為閭，五家為比鄰。

translations.literal: The present system: a hundred households form a party-chief group; twenty households a lane; five households a neighboring unit.
translations.idiomatic: The present system: a hundred households form a party-chief group; twenty households a lane; five households a neighboring unit.

sentences.zh: 百家之內，有帥二十五人，徵發皆免，苦樂不均。

translations.literal: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five chiefs exempt from levies — joy and suffering are uneven.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five chiefs exempt from levies — joy and suffering fall unevenly.

sentences.zh: 羊少狼多，復有蠶食。

translations.literal: Few sheep and many wolves — moreover there is nibbling away.
translations.idiomatic: Few sheep and many wolves — and on top of that, nibbling away.

sentences.zh: 此之為弊久矣。

translations.literal: That this is harmful has been long.
translations.idiomatic: That this is harmful has been so for a long time.

sentences.zh: 京邑諸坊，或七八百家唯一里正、二史，庶事無闕，而況外州乎？

translations.literal: In the capital's wards, some seven or eight hundred households have only one lane chief and two clerks, yet nothing is wanting in daily affairs — how much more so in the outer provinces?
translations.idiomatic: In the capital's wards, some seven or eight hundred households have only one lane chief and two clerks, yet daily affairs suffer no lack — how much more so in the outer provinces?

sentences.zh: 請依舊置三正之名不改，而百家為族，四閭，閭二比。

translations.literal: I request that the old name of Three Chiefs be kept unchanged, but a hundred households form a clan, four lanes, two neighboring units per lane.
translations.idiomatic: I request that the old name of Three Chiefs be kept unchanged, but a hundred households form a clan, with four lanes and two neighboring units per lane.

sentences.zh: 計族少十二丁，得十二疋貲絹。

translations.literal: Calculated, a clan has twelve fewer adult males — obtaining twelve bolts of compensatory silk.
translations.idiomatic: By the reckoning, each clan has twelve fewer adult males liable for service — yielding twelve bolts of compensatory silk.

sentences.zh: 略計見管之戶應二萬餘族，一歲出貲絹二十四萬疋。

translations.literal: Roughly calculated, the households under management should be over twenty thousand clans; in one year that yields two hundred forty thousand bolts of compensatory silk.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly calculated, the households under management should exceed twenty thousand clans; in one year that yields two hundred forty thousand bolts of compensatory silk.

sentences.zh: 十五丁為一番兵，計得一萬六千兵。

translations.literal: Fifteen adult males form one rotation of soldiers — calculating, one obtains sixteen thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen adult males form one rotation of soldiers — by the reckoning, one obtains sixteen thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 此富國安人之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way to enrich the state and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: This is the way to enrich the state and settle the people.

sentences.zh: 古諸侯娶九女，士一妻一妾。

translations.literal: In antiquity feudal lords married nine women; a gentleman one wife and one concubine.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity feudal lords married nine women; a gentleman took one wife and one concubine.

sentences.zh: 《晉令》：諸王置妾八人；

translations.literal: "Jin ordinance": princes may set up eight concubines;
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ordinance: princes may set up eight concubines;

sentences.zh: 郡君、侯，妾六人。

translations.literal: commandery marquises and marquises, six concubines.
translations.idiomatic: commandery marquises and marquises, six concubines.

sentences.zh: 《官品令》：第一第二品有四妾，第三第四有三妾，第五第六有二妾，第七第八有一妾。

translations.literal: "Office-rank ordinance": first and second ranks four concubines, third and fourth three, fifth and sixth two, seventh and eighth one.
translations.idiomatic: The office-rank ordinance: first and second ranks four concubines, third and fourth three, fifth and sixth two, seventh and eighth one.

sentences.zh: 所以陰教聿修，繼嗣有廣。

translations.literal: thereby the woman's instruction is thoroughly cultivated and succession broadly provided.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the instruction of women is thoroughly cultivated and succession broadly provided for.

sentences.zh: 廣繼嗣孝也，修陰教禮也。

translations.literal: Broad succession is filial; cultivating woman's instruction is ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Broad succession is filial; cultivating women's instruction is ritual.

sentences.zh: 而聖朝忽棄此數，由來漸久，將相多尚公主，王侯娶后族，故無妾媵，習以為常。

translations.literal: But the sage court suddenly abandoned these numbers; for long it has gradually worsened; generals and ministers mostly honor princesses in marriage, kings and marquises marry empress-clan women — hence no concubines; it has become customary.
translations.idiomatic: But the sage court suddenly abandoned these numbers; for a long time it has gradually worsened. Generals and ministers mostly take princesses in marriage; kings and marquises marry empress-clan women — hence there are no concubines, and it has become customary.

sentences.zh: 婦人不幸，生逢今世，舉朝既是無妾，天下殆皆一妻。

translations.literal: Alas for women — born unlucky in this age: the whole court is without concubines; under Heaven nearly all have one wife.
translations.idiomatic: Women are unfortunate to be born in this age: the whole court is without concubines, and under Heaven nearly everyone has but one wife.

sentences.zh: 設令人強志廣娶，則家道離索，身事迍邅，內外親知，共相嗤怪。

translations.literal: Suppose one with strong will took many wives — then the household would scatter, one's affairs would go badly, and kinsmen inside and out would together mock and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose someone of strong will took many wives — then the household would scatter, his affairs would go badly, and kinsmen inside and out would together mock and wonder.

sentences.zh: 凡今之人，通無準節。

translations.literal: People today universally lack standards.
translations.idiomatic: People today universally lack standards.

sentences.zh: 父母嫁女，則教以妬，姑姊逢迎，必相勸以忌。

translations.literal: When parents marry off daughters they teach jealousy; aunts and sisters in welcoming them surely urge mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When parents marry off daughters they teach jealousy; aunts and sisters, in welcoming them, surely urge mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 以制夫為婦德，以能妬為女工。

translations.literal: To control the husband is taken as wifely virtue; to be able to be jealous is taken as woman's craft.
translations.idiomatic: To control the husband is taken as wifely virtue; to be able to be jealous is taken as woman's craft.

sentences.zh: 自云不受人欺，畏他笑我。

translations.literal: They say themselves they will not be bullied by others — they fear others will laugh at them.
translations.idiomatic: They say themselves they will not be bullied by others — they fear others will laugh at them.

sentences.zh: 王公猶自一心，已下何敢二意。

translations.literal: Kings and dukes even so keep but one heart — how dare those below have two minds?
translations.idiomatic: Even kings and dukes keep but one heart — how dare those below have two minds?

sentences.zh: 夫妬忌之心生，則妻妾之禮廢，妻妾之禮廢，則姦淫之兆興，斯臣之所以毒恨者也。

translations.literal: When jealous suspicion arises, the rites between wife and concubines are abandoned; when those rites are abandoned, omens of licentiousness arise — this is what your servant bitterly hates.
translations.idiomatic: When jealous suspicion arises, the rites between wife and concubines are abandoned; when those rites are abandoned, omens of licentiousness arise — this is what your servant bitterly hates.

sentences.zh: 請以王公第一品娶八，通妻以備九女，稱事。

translations.literal: I request that for first-rank kings and dukes they marry eight, with the principal wife to complete nine women, as befits the office.
translations.idiomatic: I request that first-rank kings and dukes marry eight concubines, with the principal wife completing nine women in all, as befits the office.

sentences.zh: 二品備七，三品四品備五，五品六品則一妻二妾。

translations.literal: Second rank seven; third and fourth five; fifth and sixth one wife and two concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank, seven; third and fourth ranks, five; fifth and sixth ranks, one wife and two concubines.

sentences.zh: 限以一周，悉令充數。

translations.literal: Limited to one year, all are ordered to fill the number.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year, all are ordered to fill the number.

sentences.zh: 若不充數，及待妾非禮，使妻妬加捶撻，免所居官。

translations.literal: If they do not fill the number, or keep concubines improperly, or let the wife in jealousy add beating — dismiss them from the office they hold.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not fill the number, or keep concubines improperly, or let the wife in jealousy add beatings — dismiss them from the office they hold.

sentences.zh: 其妻無子而不娶妾，斯則自絕，無以血食祖父，請科不孝之罪，離遣其妻。

translations.literal: If the wife has no son and will not take a concubine, that is self-extinction — no blood-offering to ancestors — I request penalize with the crime of unfilial piety and divorce the wife.
translations.idiomatic: If the wife has no son and will not take a concubine, that is self-extinction — no blood-offering to ancestors. I request they be penalized with the crime of unfilial piety and the wife divorced and sent away.

sentences.zh: 臣之赤心，義唯家國，欲使吉兇無不合禮，貴賤各有其宜，省人帥以出兵丁，立倉儲以豐谷食，設賞格以擒姦盜，行典令以示朝章，庶使足食足兵，人信之矣。

translations.literal: Your servant's loyal heart, in righteousness, is only for family and state; I wish to make auspicious and inauspicious all conform to ritual, noble and base each have their proper place, reduce chief-leaders to levy soldiers, establish granaries to fill grain stores, set reward regulations to capture thieves and rebels, execute canonical statutes to display court regulations — perhaps thereby sufficient food and sufficient arms, and the people will trust.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's loyal heart, in righteousness, is only for family and state. I wish to make the auspicious and inauspicious all conform to ritual, noble and base each have their proper place, reduce chief-leaders to levy soldiers, establish granaries to fill grain stores, set reward regulations to capture thieves and rebels, and execute canonical statutes to display the court's regulations — so that there may be sufficient food and sufficient arms, and the people will trust.

sentences.zh: 又冒申妻妾之數，正欲使王侯將相功臣子弟，苗胤滿朝，傳祚無窮。

translations.literal: Again I rashly petition concerning the number of wives and concubines — my true aim is to make the sons and grandsons of kings, marquises, generals, ministers, and meritorious ministers fill the court with flourishing heirs, and transmission of the throne without end.
translations.idiomatic: Again I rashly petition concerning the number of wives and concubines — my true aim is to make the sons and grandsons of kings, marquises, generals, ministers, and meritorious ministers fill the court with flourishing heirs, so that the transmission of the throne may be without end.

sentences.zh: 此臣之志也。

translations.literal: This is this minister's aim.
translations.idiomatic: This is what your minister seeks.

sentences.zh: 詔付有司，議奏不同。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted it to the relevant offices; their memorials of deliberation differed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the relevant offices; their deliberations failed to agree.

sentences.zh: 孝友又言：「今人生為皂隸，葬擬王侯，存沒異途，無復節制。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou spoke again: "Nowadays men are born as slaves and bondsmen, yet their funerals rival those of kings and marquises; living and dead follow different paths, and restraint is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou spoke again: "Today men are born bondsmen, yet their funerals rival those of kings and marquises; in life and in death there is no restraint.

sentences.zh: 崇壯丘隴，盛飾祭儀，鄰里相榮，稱為至孝。

translations.literal: They heap up lofty mounds and tombs, lavishly adorn sacrificial rites, and neighbors take pride in one another, calling it utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: They mound tombs sky-high and lavish ritual upon ritual; neighbors boast to one another and call it supreme filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又夫婦之始，王化所先，共食合瓢，足以成禮。

translations.literal: Moreover, the beginning of husband and wife is what royal transformation puts first; sharing food and joining the gourd are enough to complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The bond of husband and wife is the first step in royal transformation; sharing a meal and drinking from one gourd are ceremony enough.

sentences.zh: 而今之富者彌奢，同牢之設，甚於祭盤，累魚成山，山有林木，林木之上，鸞鳳斯存。

translations.literal: Yet today's rich grow ever more extravagant: the arrangements for the joint wedding feast exceed sacrificial platters; fish are piled into mountains, the mountains have forest and trees, and atop the trees phoenixes perch.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rich grow ever more lavish: their joint-wedding feasts outdo sacrificial spreads — fish stacked into mountains, mountains planted with trees, and on the trees perch phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 徒有煩勞，終成委棄。

translations.literal: It is all toil for nothing; in the end it is cast away.
translations.idiomatic: All is labor wasted; in the end it is thrown away.

sentences.zh: 仰惟天意，其或不然。

translations.literal: Looking up to Heaven's intent, it may not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Surely Heaven's intent cannot be this.

sentences.zh: 請自茲以後，若婚葬過禮者，以違旨論。

translations.literal: I ask that from now on, if weddings or funerals exceed the rites, they be judged as violating the edict.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter, weddings or funerals that exceed proper rite be judged violations of the throne's intent.

sentences.zh: 官司不加糾劾，即與同罪。」

translations.literal: If officials do not investigate and impeach, they share the crime."
translations.idiomatic: Officials who fail to investigate and impeach shall share the guilt."

sentences.zh: 孝友在尹積年，以法自守，甚著聲稱，然性無骨鯁，善事權勢，為正直者所譏。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou accumulated years as mayor of Yin, held to the law himself, and won great repute; yet by nature he lacked backbone, was skilled at serving the powerful, and was mocked by the upright.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou held office in Yin for many years, kept to the law, and won great repute; yet he lacked backbone, was adept at courting the powerful, and upright men scorned him for it.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，準例降爵，封臨淮縣公，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao of Qi, by precedent his rank was reduced; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linhuai county and appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Qi Tianbao, by precedent his rank was lowered; he was made duke of Linhuai county and appointed grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，被詔入晉陽宮，出與元暉業同被害。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year he was summoned by edict into Jinyang Palace and, on leaving, was killed together with Yuan Huiye.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year he was summoned by edict to Jinyang Palace; on leaving he was killed together with Yuan Huiye.

sentences.zh: 元暉業，字紹遠，魏景穆皇帝之玄孫。

translations.literal: Yuan Huiye, styled Shaoyuan, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Jingmu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huiye, styled Shaoyuan, was a great-great-grandson of Emperor Jingmu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 少險薄，多與寇盜交通。

translations.literal: In youth he was crafty and mean, and often associated with bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was mean and unscrupulous and kept company with bandits.

sentences.zh: 長乃變節，涉子史，亦頗屬文，而慷慨有志節。

translations.literal: When grown he changed his ways, studied the Masters and histories, was also rather skilled at composition, and was ardent in spirit and aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he mended his ways, took up the Masters and histories, wrote passable prose, and bore himself with generous resolve.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太尉，加特進，領中書監，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, was given the supernumerary rank, headed the Secretariat Supervisor, and recorded affairs for the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of works and grand commandant, was given supernumerary rank, headed the secretariat, and recorded affairs for the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 文襄嘗問之曰：「此何所披覽？

translations.literal: Gao Cheng once asked him: "What are you perusing here?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng once asked him, "What are you reading?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「數尋伊、霍之傳，不讀曹、馬之書。」

translations.literal: " He replied: "I often seek the biographies of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of Cao [Cao] and the Sima [clan]."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I pore over the lives of Yi Yin and Huo Guang — not the chronicles of Cao Cao and the Sima clan."

sentences.zh: 暉業以時運漸謝，不復圖全，唯事飲啖，一日一羊，三日一犢。

translations.literal: Huiye, seeing the times gradually decline, no longer plotted for survival; he devoted himself only to eating and drinking — one sheep a day, one calf every three days.
translations.idiomatic: As the times waned, Huiye ceased to plot for his own survival; he gave himself only to eating and drinking — a sheep each day, a calf every three days.

sentences.zh: 又嘗賦詩云：「昔居王道泰，濟濟富群英；

translations.literal: Again he once composed verse: "In old days we dwelt when the royal way was at peace, teeming with hosts of worthies;
translations.idiomatic: He once composed verse: "In old days we dwelt when the royal way was at peace, teeming with hosts of worthies;

sentences.zh: 今逢世路阻，狐兔鬱縱橫。

translations.literal: Today we meet blocked roads in the world; foxes and hares throng the crossways."
translations.idiomatic: Today the road is blocked; foxes and hares throng the crossways."

sentences.zh: 」齊初，降封美陽縣公，開府儀同三司、特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was reduced in rank to Duke of Meiyang county, given the insignia Opening Office, Equal in Honor to the Three Offices, and made Supernumerary.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Qi he was lowered to duke of Meiyang county, with opening office equal in honor to the three highest offices and supernumerary rank.

sentences.zh: 暉業之在晉陽也，無所交通，居常閑暇，乃撰魏藩王家世，號為《辯宗錄》，四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: While Huiye was at Jinyang he had no associations; in his usual leisure he composed the lineages of Wei imperial princes, titled "Records for Distinguishing Clans," forty juan, and it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang, Huiye kept to himself. In his leisure he compiled the genealogies of Wei's imperial princes under the title "Records for Distinguishing Clans," forty juan, and it circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 位望隆重，又以性氣不倫，每被忌。

translations.literal: His position and prestige were weighty; moreover, because his temperament was unlike others, he was often resented.
translations.idiomatic: His rank and repute were weighty, yet his temperament set him apart and he was often resented.

sentences.zh: 天保二年，從駕至晉陽，於宮門外罵元韶曰：「爾不及一老嫗，背負璽與人，何不打碎之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao, following the imperial carriage to Jinyang, outside the palace gate he reviled Yuan Shao: "You are not equal to an old woman — you carried the seal on your back and gave it to another; why did you not smash it?
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year two, while following the imperial carriage to Jinyang, he reviled Yuan Shao outside the palace gate: "You are worse than an old crone — you bore the seal on your back and handed it to another. Why not have smashed it?

sentences.zh: 我出此言，卽知死也，然爾亦詎得幾時！

translations.literal: I speak these words knowing I shall die — yet how much longer will you have!"
translations.idiomatic: I speak this knowing I shall die — but how much longer will you last?"

sentences.zh: 」文宣聞而殺之，亦斬臨淮公孝友。

translations.literal: When Gao Yang heard of it he had him killed and also beheaded Duke of Linhuai Xiaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang heard and had him killed; he also beheaded Duke of Linhuai Xiaoyou.

sentences.zh: 孝友臨刑，驚惶失措，暉業神色自若。

translations.literal: Facing execution, Xiaoyou was panic-stricken and at a loss; Huiye's bearing was calm.
translations.idiomatic: At the block Xiaoyou panicked; Huiye's bearing never changed.

sentences.zh: 仍鑿冰沉其屍。

translations.literal: They then cut ice and sank their corpses.
translations.idiomatic: Their bodies were sunk through holes cut in the ice.

sentences.zh: 暉業弟昭業，頗有學問，位諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was quite learned and held the post of Grand Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was a scholar of some note and rose to grand adviser.

sentences.zh: 莊帝幸洛南，昭業立於閶闔門外叩馬諫，帝避之而過，後勞勉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang visited the south of Luo, Zhaoye stood outside the Changhe Gate, seized the horse's bridle, and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed by, but later commended and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang visited south Luo, Zhaoye stood outside Changhe Gate, seized the bridle, and remonstrated. The emperor avoided him and rode on, but later commended him.

sentences.zh: 位給事黃門侍郎、衛將軍，右光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: He rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, General of the Guard, and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate, general of the guard, and right grand master for splendid happiness, and died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Marquis Cultured.

sentences.zh: 元弼，字輔宗，魏司空暉之子。

translations.literal: Yuan Bi, styled Fuzong, was son of Hui, Minister of Works of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bi, styled Fuzong, was son of Hui, minister of works of Wei.

sentences.zh: 性剛正，有文學。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and upright and possessed literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and learned.

sentences.zh: 位中散大夫。

translations.literal: He held the post of Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 以世嫡應襲先爵。

translations.literal: As heir of the main line he should have inherited his predecessor's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: As heir of the main line he should have inherited the family enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 為季父尚書僕射麗因于氏親寵，遂奪弼王爵，橫授同母兄子誕，於是弼絕棄人事，托疾還私第。

translations.literal: But his younger uncle Li, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, through the Yu clan's favor in kinship, thereupon seized Bi's princely rank and arbitrarily granted it to his elder uterine brother's son Dan; Bi then abandoned human affairs, feigned illness, and returned to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Li, vice director of the masters of writing, used the Yu clan's favor at court to strip Bi of his princely rank and grant it to his uterine brother's son Dan. Bi thereupon withdrew from public life, pleaded illness, and retired to his private residence.

sentences.zh: 宣武中為侍中，弼上表固讓。

translations.literal: In Xuanwu's time he was made Palace Attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was made palace attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.

sentences.zh: 入嵩山，以穴為室，布衣蔬食，卒。

translations.literal: He entered Mount Song, took a cave for his chamber, wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Mount Song, made a cave his home, wore hemp and ate greens, and died.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，子暉業訴復王爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year one his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，追贈尚書令、司徒公，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an, posthumously he was given Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an year three he was posthumously made director of the masters of writing and duke of the department of state affairs, with the posthumous title Cultured and Offering.

sentences.zh: 初，弼嘗夢人謂之曰：「君身不得傳世封，其紹先爵者，君長子紹遠也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bi once dreamed that someone told him: "Your person will not transmit the enfeoffment of the age; he who will continue the former rank is your eldest son Shaoyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bi had dreamed that someone told him, "You will not pass the enfeoffment down in your own lifetime; your eldest son Shaoyuan will restore the former rank."

sentences.zh: 」弼覺，即告暉業，終如其言。

translations.literal: When Bi awoke he at once told Huiye, and in the end it was as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi awoke he told Huiye at once, and in the end it proved true.

sentences.zh: 韶性行溫裕，以高氏婿，頗膺時寵。

translations.literal: Shao by nature and conduct was mild and generous; as son-in-law of the Gao clan he enjoyed considerable favor of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was mild and generous by nature; as a son-in-law of the Gaos he enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 能自謙退，臨人有惠政。

translations.literal: He could humble himself and yield; in governing men he had policies of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He knew how to yield; in office he governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 好儒學，禮致才彥。

translations.literal: He loved Confucian learning and with ritual received men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved Confucian learning and with proper ceremony welcomed men of talent.

sentences.zh: 愛林泉，修第宅，華而不侈。

translations.literal: He loved forests and springs, built mansions and residences — splendid yet not extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: He loved forests and springs and built mansions splendid but not extravagant.

sentences.zh: 文宣帝剃韶鬚髯，加以粉黛，衣婦人服以自隨曰：「我以彭城為嬪御。

translations.literal: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard and whiskers, applied powder and rouge, dressed him in women's garments to keep at his side, saying: "I take Pengcheng as my palace woman."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang shaved Shao's beard, painted his face, dressed him in women's clothes and kept him at his side, saying, "I take Prince of Pengcheng as my consort."

sentences.zh: 」譏元氏微弱，比之婦女。

translations.literal: He mocked the weakness of the Yuan clan, comparing them to women.
translations.idiomatic: He mocked the Yuan for their weakness, likening them to women.

sentences.zh: 十年，太史奏云：「今年當除舊布新。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Grand Astrologer memorialized: "This year old shall be removed and new spread."
translations.idiomatic: In year ten the grand astrologer reported, "This year the old must yield to the new."

sentences.zh: 」文宣謂韶曰：「漢光武何故中興？

translations.literal: Gao Yang said to Shao: "Why did Han Guangwu restore the dynasty?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang asked Shao, "Why did Emperor Guangwu of Han restore the dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 」韶曰：「為誅諸劉不盡。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Because the Liu were not all killed."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Because the Liu were not all killed."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃誅諸元以厭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed the various Yuan to satisfy the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they slaughtered the Yuan to satisfy the omen.

sentences.zh: 遂以五月誅元世哲、景武等二十五家，餘十九家並禁止之。

translations.literal: Then in the fifth month they executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under restraint.

sentences.zh: 韶幽於京畿地牢，絕食，啖衣袖而死。

translations.literal: Shao was imprisoned in the capital-district dungeon, denied food, and died gnawing his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was imprisoned in the capital dungeon, denied food, and died gnawing his sleeves.

sentences.zh: 及七月，大誅元氏，自昭成已下並無遺焉。

translations.literal: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Zhaocheng down, none were spared.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month came the great slaughter of the Yuan; from Emperor Zhaocheng down, none were spared.

sentences.zh: 或父祖為王，或身常貴顯，或兄弟強壯，皆斬東市。

translations.literal: Some had fathers or grandfathers who were kings, some had themselves long held high rank, some had brothers in their prime — all were beheaded at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had themselves long held high rank, some had brothers in their prime — all were beheaded at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 其嬰兒投於空中，承之以矟。

translations.literal: Their infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.
translations.idiomatic: Their infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.

sentences.zh: 前後死者凡七百二十一人，悉投屍漳水，剖魚多得爪甲，都下為之久不食魚。

translations.literal: In all, before and after, seven hundred twenty-one died; all corpses were cast into the Zhang River. When fish were gutted many claws and nails were found; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred twenty-one died in all; every corpse was cast into the Zhang River. When fish were gutted, claws and nails were found inside; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：元氏蕃熾，馮茲慶靈。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Yuan clan flourished in abundance, relying on this auspicious numen.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The Yuan clan flourished in full vigor, blessed by fate's favor.

sentences.zh: 道隨終運，命偶淫刑。

translations.literal: The Way followed the ending fortune; their fate met wanton punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Way waned with the dynasty's end; their lives met cruel and lawless punishment.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The complete text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972.
